meta.note: Original CISSP-style practice questions. matching questions carry a prompts[] (left items numbered 1..n) and options[] (right items A..n); correct_answer encodes the pairing. sequence_ordering correct_answer lists option labels in correct order.

questions.question: The KEY functional difference between an IDS and an IPS is that an IPS:

options.label: A
options.text: Is a physical lock on the server room

options.label: B
options.text: Only logs events and never alerts

options.label: C
options.text: Can actively block/stop detected malicious traffic, not just alert on it

explanation.why_correct: An IDS detects and alerts on suspicious activity; an IPS can additionally take preventive action (block/drop) inline to stop the threat.

why_others_are_wrong.B: An IDS does alert; the distinction is the IPS's ability to actively block.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Both detect intrusions; the IPS also prevents.
why_others_are_wrong.A: IDS/IPS are logical controls, not physical locks.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes IPS (prevent/block) from IDS (detect/alert).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > IDS/IPS Systems

questions.question: An organization wants its IDS to catch brand-new, never-before-seen attacks (not just known ones). Which detection method is MOST suitable, and what is its main drawback?

options.label: A
options.text: Signature-based detection; it cannot be updated

options.label: B
options.text: Signature-based detection; it never needs updates

options.label: C
options.text: Behavior/anomaly-based detection; it is prone to false positives and needs a baseline learning period

options.label: D
options.text: Behavior-based detection; it can only detect known signatures

explanation.why_correct: Behavior/anomaly-based detection compares activity to a learned baseline of "normal," so it can flag novel attacks—but it is prone to false positives and requires a learning period.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Signature-based detection only catches known patterns and does require updates.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Behavior-based detection is precisely what catches unknown (non-signature) activity.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Signature-based detection requires constant updates for new threats.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps novel-attack detection to anomaly-based (with false-positive drawback).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Detection Types

questions.question: Knowledge-based (signature-based) intrusion detection works by:

options.label: A
options.text: Learning a baseline of normal behavior over time

options.label: C
options.text: Matching activity against a database of known attack patterns/signatures

explanation.why_correct: Signature/knowledge-based detection (pattern matching) compares observed activity to known attack signatures and requires constant updates to detect emerging threats.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Learning a baseline of normal is behavior/anomaly-based detection.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Signature detection is targeted, not random.
why_others_are_wrong.B: It detects patterns; it does not encrypt packets.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps known-pattern matching to signature-based detection.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Detection Types

questions.question: A limitation of a Host-Based IDS (HIDS) compared to a Network-Based IDS (NIDS) is that the HIDS:

options.label: B
options.text: Is unable to detect file changes

options.label: C
options.text: Cannot analyze network-wide threats; it only monitors activity on its own host

explanation.why_correct: A HIDS monitors a specific host's activity but cannot see network-level threats or misconfigurations across the network—that is the NIDS's role.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Monitoring host activity is exactly what a HIDS does.
why_others_are_wrong.B: HIDS can detect host file/integrity changes.
why_others_are_wrong.D: HIDS is not limited to wireless networks.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the host-scope limitation of HIDS vs NIDS.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Host-Based IDS (HIDS) and Host-Based IPS (HIPS)

questions.question: Stateful protocol analysis detection identifies threats by:

options.label: B
options.text: Comparing observed events against expected protocol states using vendor signature profiles

options.label: D
options.text: Learning a statistical baseline of user behavior

explanation.why_correct: Stateful protocol analysis evaluates events against the known/expected states of a communication protocol (using vendor-provided profiles) to detect protocol anomalies.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Simple string matching describes basic signature detection.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Statistical baselining of behavior is anomaly-based detection.
why_others_are_wrong.C: It analyzes protocol state; it does not block everything by default.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps protocol-state analysis to stateful protocol analysis.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Stateful Protocol Analysis

questions.question: A honeypot is primarily deployed to:

options.label: B
options.text: Provide backup power to the data center

options.label: C
options.text: Lure and observe attackers using a decoy system, diverting them from real assets

explanation.why_correct: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to attract attackers so their methods can be studied and they are diverted from real production systems (a honeynet is a network of honeypots).

why_others_are_wrong.B: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: A honeypot is a decoy, not a database-encryption tool.
why_others_are_wrong.A: A honeypot complements, not replaces, a firewall.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the decoy/observation purpose of honeypots.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Honeypots and Honeynets

questions.question: A high-security environment wants to allow ONLY explicitly approved applications to run and block everything else. Which approach fits, and what is it also called?

explanation.why_correct: Whitelisting permits only specified actions/applications and denies everything else by default ("permit by exception")—stricter and more secure, ideal for high-security needs.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Blacklisting allows everything except listed items (less strict).
why_others_are_wrong.A: Blacklisting is "deny by exception," not "permit by exception."
why_others_are_wrong.C: Whitelisting denies by default, not allows everything.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps allow-only-approved to whitelisting ("permit by exception").

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Whitelisting

questions.question: Blacklisting ("deny by exception") is characterized by:

options.label: A
options.text: Blocking all traffic with no exceptions

options.label: D
options.text: Denying specific listed items and allowing everything else by default

explanation.why_correct: Blacklisting denies specific actions/items while allowing everything else by default—less secure than whitelisting but favors availability.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Allowing only approved items is whitelisting.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Blacklisting allows non-listed items; it does not block everything.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Encryption is unrelated to blacklisting.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the allow-by-default nature of blacklisting.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Blacklisting

questions.question: Sandboxing (confinement) protects systems by:

options.label: D
options.text: Running code in an isolated environment so it cannot affect the rest of the system

explanation.why_correct: Sandboxing/confinement isolates code execution so untrusted or suspicious software cannot harm the host or other systems.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Redundant power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Packet routing is a network function.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Certificate issuance is a PKI/CA function.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of sandboxing/confinement.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Sandboxing

questions.question: Separation (segregation) of duties in security operations primarily:

options.label: A
options.text: Prevents any single individual from compromising security controls by dividing responsibilities

options.label: B
options.text: Gives one administrator full control for efficiency

options.label: C
options.text: Allows users to approve their own changes

explanation.why_correct: Separation of duties divides responsibilities so no single person can both perform and conceal a malicious or erroneous action—reducing fraud and conflict of interest.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Concentrating control in one person defeats SoD.
why_others_are_wrong.D: SoD does not remove logging requirements.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Self-approval undermines the control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the fraud-prevention purpose of SoD.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Separation or Segregation of Duties

questions.question: A finance department rotates staff through different roles every few months. Besides cross-training, what security BENEFIT does job rotation provide?

options.label: A
options.text: It can expose fraud/errors that a single person could otherwise hide over time

options.label: C
options.text: It permanently removes the need for separation of duties

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees no employee will ever leave

explanation.why_correct: Job rotation makes it harder for one person to conceal ongoing fraud/errors (a successor may discover it) and reduces dependence on any single individual.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Job rotation complements, not replaces, separation of duties.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Rotation does not control attrition.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Rotation does not perform database encryption.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the fraud-detection benefit of job rotation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Job Rotation

questions.question: Privileged account management in security operations focuses on:

options.label: A
options.text: Providing fire suppression in the data center

options.label: C
options.text: Controlling and monitoring the use of elevated/administrative accounts

explanation.why_correct: Privileged account management controls, restricts, and monitors elevated accounts because they are high-value targets and high-impact if misused.

why_others_are_wrong.D: IP assignment is DHCP's function.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Fire suppression is a physical control.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Wireless encryption is WPA2/WPA3.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the elevated-account focus of privileged account management.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Privileged Account Management

questions.subtopic: Need to know vs least privilege
questions.question: In the guide's framing, how does least privilege differ in emphasis from need-to-know?

options.label: A
options.text: Need-to-know applies only to wireless networks

options.label: B
options.text: Least privilege focuses on functional access (what you can do); need-to-know focuses on data access (what you can see)

options.label: D
options.text: Least privilege grants maximum access; need-to-know grants none

explanation.why_correct: The guide notes least privilege emphasizes functional access rights, while need-to-know restricts access to specific data/information required for duties.

why_others_are_wrong.C: They are related but distinct in emphasis (function vs data).
why_others_are_wrong.D: Least privilege grants minimum, not maximum, access.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Need-to-know is not limited to wireless networks.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes least privilege (function) from need-to-know (data).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Security Operation Concepts

questions.question: Which TWO are PREVENTATIVE controls (designed to stop violations before they occur)? (Select TWO.)

options.label: B
options.text: Reviewing IDS alert logs after an event

explanation.why_correct: Whitelisting and a blocking firewall prevent violations before they happen; reviewing logs/alerts after the fact is detective.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Reviewing alert logs after an event is a detective activity.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Analyzing logs during an investigation is detective/forensic.

questions.exam_reasoning: Separates preventative from detective controls.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Detective and Preventative Concepts

questions.question: Match each IDS detection method (1-3) to its description (A-C).

options.label: A
options.text: Matches activity against a database of known attack patterns

options.label: B
options.text: Evaluates events against expected protocol states

options.label: C
options.text: Compares activity to a learned baseline of normal behavior

explanation.why_correct: Signature-based → known attack patterns (B); Anomaly-based → baseline of normal (A); Stateful protocol analysis → expected protocol states (C).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests mapping of IDS detection methods.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Detection Types

questions.question: A Network-Based IPS (NIPS) is BEST positioned to:

options.label: B
options.text: Monitor only a single host's file integrity

options.label: C
options.text: Monitor and block malicious traffic across network segments inline

explanation.why_correct: A NIPS sits inline on the network to monitor and actively block malicious traffic across segments network-wide.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Single-host file integrity monitoring is a HIDS/HIPS function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Credential issuance is an IAM function.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the network-wide inline role of NIPS.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > IDS and IPS Deployment Types

questions.question: When using third-party security services, a key best practice is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Assume they need no contractual security requirements

options.label: B
options.text: Give them unrestricted access with no oversight

options.label: C
options.text: Integrate their roles into the incident response plan, covering both detection and prevention

options.label: D
options.text: Exclude them entirely from any incident planning

explanation.why_correct: Third-party providers should be integrated into the incident response plan with defined roles in detection and prevention, and governed by appropriate contracts/SLAs.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Unrestricted, unmonitored access is a major risk.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Excluding them from planning leaves gaps if they are involved operationally.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Contractual security requirements (SLAs) are essential for third parties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests integrating third parties into incident response planning.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Third-Party Involvement in Incident Response

questions.question: A "padded cell" works alongside an IDS by:

options.label: A
options.text: Transferring a detected attacker into an isolated, simulated environment in real time

explanation.why_correct: A padded cell is a protected, isolated environment that an IDS redirects an attacker into once detected, containing them away from real systems.

why_others_are_wrong.D: It isolates, not destroys, the attacker's device.
why_others_are_wrong.B: It is a containment environment, not an encryption tool.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Redundant power is unrelated to a padded cell.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the IDS-triggered isolation role of a padded cell.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Advanced Honeypot Deployment

questions.question: After deploying an anomaly-based IDS, the SOC is flooded with alerts for legitimate-but-unusual activity. The MOST likely cause is:

options.label: A
options.text: The IDS only uses known signatures

options.label: B
options.text: The network has no traffic at all

options.label: C
options.text: The IDS is a physical access control

options.label: D
options.text: False positives from an immature/insufficient baseline of normal behavior

explanation.why_correct: Anomaly-based detection is prone to false positives, especially before the baseline of normal behavior is well established (the learning period).

why_others_are_wrong.A: Signature-only detection would not flag unusual-but-unknown activity as anomalies.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Alerts indicate there is traffic to analyze.
why_others_are_wrong.C: An IDS is a logical control, not a physical access control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps anomaly-detection alert floods to false positives/baseline immaturity.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Behavior-Based Detection (Anomaly-Based)

questions.question: Applying least privilege in security operations means:

options.label: A
options.text: Granting subjects only the access required to perform their job functions

explanation.why_correct: Least privilege grants only the minimum access necessary, limiting the damage from compromise or misuse.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Universal admin rights violate least privilege.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Anonymous access undermines accountability.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Removing access controls is the opposite of least privilege.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of least privilege in operations.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Security Operation Concepts

questions.question: Which is an example of a DETECTIVE control?

options.label: A
options.text: Application whitelisting that prevents unapproved software

options.label: B
options.text: An IDS that alerts on suspicious activity

options.label: C
options.text: A locked door that stops entry

options.label: D
options.text: A firewall that blocks unauthorized ports

explanation.why_correct: Detective controls identify/announce that an event has occurred (e.g., an IDS alert); the others prevent events from occurring.

why_others_are_wrong.D: A blocking firewall is preventative.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Whitelisting is preventative.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A locked door is a preventative physical control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes detective (alert) from preventative controls.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Detective and Preventative Concepts

questions.question: A Wireless IDS (WIDS) is specifically designed to:

options.label: A
options.text: Monitor only wired host file integrity

options.label: C
options.text: Monitor wireless network traffic for protocol-related anomalies (e.g., rogue APs)

explanation.why_correct: A WIDS monitors wireless traffic for anomalies such as rogue access points and wireless-specific attacks.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Wired host file integrity is a HIDS concern.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Generator power is unrelated.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Email encryption is S/MIME/PGP.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the wireless focus of a WIDS.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Wireless IDS and Wireless IPS

questions.question: Layered security (defense in depth) against malware means:

options.label: A
options.text: Disabling all security to improve performance

options.label: B
options.text: Relying on one antivirus product alone

options.label: D
options.text: Using multiple, overlapping controls so no single failure leads to compromise

explanation.why_correct: Defense in depth layers multiple controls (e.g., anti-malware, awareness training, filtering) so the failure of one does not result in compromise.

why_others_are_wrong.B: A single control is the opposite of layered defense.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Disabling security increases risk.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Encrypting a logo provides no meaningful protection.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of layered defense against malware.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Defense Mechanisms Against Malware

questions.question: A single administrator can create user accounts AND approve their own access requests AND clear the audit logs. Which principle is violated, and what is the risk?

options.label: B
options.text: Separation of duties; one person could grant and hide unauthorized access

options.label: C
options.text: Least common mechanism; too many shared components

options.label: D
options.text: Defense in depth; the network is too segmented

explanation.why_correct: Concentrating account creation, approval, and log-clearing in one person violates separation of duties—enabling that person to grant and conceal unauthorized access.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Defense in depth concerns layered controls, not this concentration of duties.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Least common mechanism concerns shared components, not duty concentration.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Fail-secure concerns failure behavior, not duty separation.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps concentrated conflicting duties to an SoD violation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Separation or Segregation of Duties

questions.question: The KEY difference between a worm and a virus is that a worm:

options.label: A
options.text: Self-propagates across networks without needing a host file or user action

options.label: B
options.text: Always requires a user to open an infected file

explanation.why_correct: A worm self-replicates and spreads across networks on its own, whereas a virus typically needs to attach to a host file and rely on user action to spread.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Requiring a user to open a file describes a virus, not a worm.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Worms spread between systems—that is their hallmark.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Encrypting files for ransom describes ransomware.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes self-propagating worms from host-dependent viruses.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware

questions.question: A logic bomb is malware that:

options.label: A
options.text: Executes its malicious payload when a specific condition or trigger is met

options.label: D
options.text: Provides remote control of a device

explanation.why_correct: A logic bomb lies dormant until a defined condition/trigger (date, event, action) is met, then executes its payload.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Immediate self-propagation describes a worm.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Remote control describes a RAT.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Unwanted ads describe adware.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps condition-triggered execution to a logic bomb.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware

questions.question: A Remote Access Trojan (RAT) primarily enables an attacker to:

options.label: C
options.text: Gain covert remote control over an infected device

explanation.why_correct: A RAT gives an attacker covert remote control of the infected system, often for surveillance, data theft, or lateral movement.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Revenue-generating ads describe adware.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Clock synchronization is NTP.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps covert remote control to a RAT.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware

questions.question: A polymorphic virus is difficult for signature-based antivirus to detect because it:

options.label: A
options.text: Changes its code/appearance with each infection to evade signature matching

options.label: D
options.text: Always uses the exact same byte pattern

explanation.why_correct: A polymorphic virus mutates its code/signature on each infection, defeating static signature matching and requiring heuristic/behavioral detection.

why_others_are_wrong.D: A constant byte pattern would be easy to signature-match.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Polymorphic viruses do replicate (while mutating).
why_others_are_wrong.B: They are not limited to wireless networks.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps signature evasion via mutation to polymorphic viruses.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Viruses by Behavior

questions.question: A macro virus typically spreads through:

options.label: D
options.text: Malicious macros embedded in documents (e.g., word processor/spreadsheet files)

explanation.why_correct: A macro virus is written in the macro language of applications and embeds in documents, executing when the document is opened with macros enabled.

why_others_are_wrong.A: MBR infection describes a master boot record virus.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Macro viruses spread via documents, not only wireless.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Door locks are physical controls.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps document-macro infection to macro viruses.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Virus Types by Infection Method

questions.question: An antivirus product scans every file the moment it is opened or executed. Which scanning mode is this, and how does it differ from the alternative?

options.label: A
options.text: On-demand scanning; it only runs once a year

options.label: B
options.text: On-access scanning; it checks files in real time as they are used, vs on-demand which runs on a schedule/manually

options.label: C
options.text: On-access scanning; it never checks files in real time

options.label: D
options.text: On-demand scanning; it scans every file as it opens

explanation.why_correct: On-access scanning inspects files in real time as they are accessed/executed; on-demand scanning runs on a schedule or when manually initiated.

why_others_are_wrong.A: On-demand is not limited to yearly; and the scenario describes real-time access.
why_others_are_wrong.C: On-access does check in real time—that defines it.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Real-time-as-opened is on-access, not on-demand.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes on-access (real-time) from on-demand (scheduled/manual) scanning.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware Scanning

questions.question: Heuristic (behavior-based) malware analysis improves on pure signature detection by:

options.label: A
options.text: Identifying suspicious behavior/characteristics, helping catch new or unknown malware

explanation.why_correct: Heuristic analysis evaluates code behavior/characteristics (statically or dynamically) to flag previously unseen malware that lacks a known signature.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Exact-signature matching is the limitation heuristics overcome.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Heuristics involve analysis, not its absence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Detection does not encrypt the files.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps unknown-malware detection to heuristic analysis.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Anti-Malware

questions.question: When antivirus software isolates an infected file so it cannot execute or spread, but does not delete it, this action is called:

explanation.why_correct: Quarantine isolates the suspicious/infected file (preventing execution/spread) while preserving it for review or recovery.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Disinfect attempts to clean the malware from the file.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Delete removes the file entirely.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Encrypt is not an anti-malware response function here.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the quarantine function.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Anti-Malware Functions

questions.question: Match each malware type (1-4) to its description (A-D).

options.label: B
options.text: Encrypts data and demands payment for the key

options.label: C
options.text: Malicious software disguised as a legitimate program

options.label: D
options.text: A network of compromised devices controlled by an attacker

explanation.why_correct: Ransomware → encrypts for ransom (B); Keylogger → records keystrokes (A); Trojan horse → disguised malware (D); Botnet → network of compromised devices (C).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests mapping of malware types to descriptions.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware

questions.question: A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system primarily:

options.label: A
options.text: Provides backup power to the data center

options.label: B
options.text: Aggregates and correlates logs/events from many sources for centralized analysis and alerting

explanation.why_correct: A SIEM centralizes log/event collection, correlation, and alerting across the environment, supporting detection and investigation.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Physical guarding is a facility control.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Wireless encryption is WPA2/WPA3.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the central log aggregation/correlation role of SIEM.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

questions.question: Order these stages of the Cyber Kill Chain as an intrusion progresses. (Provide the option labels in order.)

explanation.why_correct: The Cyber Kill Chain runs: Reconnaissance, Weaponization, Delivery, Exploitation, Installation, Command and Control, and Actions on Objectives.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the ordered Cyber Kill Chain stages.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Cyber Kill Chain

questions.question: The MITRE ATT&CK framework is BEST described as:

options.label: B
options.text: A knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs)

options.label: D
options.text: A type of fire suppression system

explanation.why_correct: MITRE ATT&CK catalogs real-world adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, used for threat modeling, detection engineering, and defense.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Wireless encryption standards are WPA2/WPA3.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Fire suppression is a physical control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps adversary TTP knowledge base to MITRE ATT&CK.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > MITRE ATT&CK Framework

questions.question: A SOC is overwhelmed by repetitive alert triage. Which technology automates and orchestrates response workflows (runbooks) to reduce manual effort?

explanation.why_correct: SOAR orchestrates and automates response workflows (runbooks/playbooks) across tools, reducing repetitive manual work and speeding response.

why_others_are_wrong.A: A cold site is a DR recovery facility.
why_others_are_wrong.D: A padded cell isolates attackers, not automates SOC workflows.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A UPS provides backup power.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps automated/orchestrated response workflows to SOAR.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR)

questions.question: User Behavior Analytics (UBA) helps detect threats by:

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing baselines of normal user activity and flagging anomalous behavior (e.g., insider threats)

explanation.why_correct: UBA models normal user behavior and flags deviations (e.g., unusual access patterns), aiding detection of compromised accounts and insider threats.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Data-at-rest encryption is a separate control.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Packet routing is a network function.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Generator power is unrelated.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the anomalous-user-behavior detection of UBA.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Behavior Analytics

questions.question: To preserve the integrity and usefulness of logs for monitoring, an organization should:

options.label: A
options.text: Disable logging to save disk space

options.label: B
options.text: Allow every user to edit log files

options.label: C
options.text: Store logs only on the system that generated them

options.label: D
options.text: Centralize logs on protected servers and restrict who can modify them

explanation.why_correct: Centralizing logs on protected/remote servers with restricted modification protects against tampering and supports reliable monitoring and investigation.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Universal edit rights destroy log integrity.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Local-only logs can be altered/destroyed by an attacker on that host.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Disabling logging eliminates the audit trail.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests centralized, protected log storage.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Protecting Log Files

questions.question: Threat intelligence primarily helps an organization to:

options.label: B
options.text: Make informed, proactive security decisions using analyzed information about threats and TTPs

explanation.why_correct: Threat intelligence gathers and analyzes information about threats/TTPs to support proactive, informed defensive decisions.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Redundant power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: IP assignment is DHCP's function.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Website encryption is TLS/HTTPS.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the proactive-decision value of threat intelligence.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Threat Intelligence

questions.question: The PRIMARY security purpose of a formal change control process is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure changes are reviewed/approved so they do not introduce misconfigurations or security incidents

options.label: C
options.text: Allow any administrator to change production without review

options.label: D
options.text: Speed up changes by skipping testing

explanation.why_correct: Change control provides structured review/approval of updates and configuration changes, maintaining security and preventing misconfigurations or incidents.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Unreviewed production changes are exactly what change control prevents.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Change control does not remove the need for backups.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Skipping testing increases the risk of incidents.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the review/approval purpose of change control.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > Change Control

questions.question: In configuration management, a secure baseline configuration serves as:

options.label: A
options.text: A documented reference for consistent, secure deployment of configuration items

options.label: C
options.text: A list of employees authorized to take vacation

explanation.why_correct: A secure baseline defines a known-good configuration for each configuration item (CI), used as a reference for consistent, secure deployments and drift detection.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Vacation lists are unrelated to configuration baselines.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Generator schedules are power-management items.
why_others_are_wrong.B: A wireless key is a network secret, not a config baseline.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the role of a secure configuration baseline.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > Implementation Phase

questions.question: Order the four main phases of security-focused configuration management (NIST SP 800-128). (Provide the option labels in order.)

explanation.why_correct: NIST SP 800-128 configuration management proceeds: Planning, Identifying/Implementing configurations, Controlling changes, and Monitoring.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the ordered configuration management phases.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > Configuration Management

questions.question: Patch management primarily reduces risk by:

options.label: C
options.text: Applying vendor updates to fix known vulnerabilities in a controlled way

explanation.why_correct: Patch management deploys updates to remediate known vulnerabilities, ideally tested and rolled out through change control to avoid disruption.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Traffic encryption is a separate control.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Backup power is a UPS/generator function.
why_others_are_wrong.D: IP assignment is DHCP's function.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the vulnerability-remediation purpose of patch management.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > System Patch Management

questions.question: A critical patch is released. Before deploying it broadly to production, the BEST practice is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Disable patching entirely to avoid downtime

options.label: B
options.text: Push it to all production systems immediately with no testing

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore it until the next annual review

options.label: D
options.text: Test the patch in a non-production environment and deploy via change control

explanation.why_correct: Patches should be tested in a representative non-production environment and rolled out through change control to balance security with stability.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Untested mass deployment risks outages from a faulty patch.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Delaying critical patches leaves known vulnerabilities exposed.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Disabling patching leaves systems vulnerable indefinitely.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests test-then-deploy patch practice.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > System Patch Management

questions.question: Media management as part of configuration/operations involves:

options.label: D
options.text: Protecting and controlling physical and digital media (e.g., drives, tapes, cloud storage)

explanation.why_correct: Media management secures and controls physical and digital media—hard drives, backup tapes, and cloud storage—across their lifecycle.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Marketing campaigns are unrelated.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Lunch scheduling is unrelated.
why_others_are_wrong.B: BGP routing is a network function.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the scope of media management.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > Media Management

questions.question: Ransomware has encrypted files on several endpoints. Which combination BEST supports recovery WITHOUT paying the ransom?

options.label: A
options.text: Paying immediately to guarantee data return

options.label: B
options.text: Disabling all backups to save space

options.label: C
options.text: Isolating affected systems and restoring from clean, tested offline backups

options.label: D
options.text: Connecting all systems together to share the decryptor

explanation.why_correct: Containing the spread (isolation) and restoring from clean, tested, offline backups enables recovery without funding criminals or trusting attacker-provided keys.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Paying does not guarantee recovery and encourages further attacks.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Interconnecting systems risks spreading the ransomware further.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Disabling backups removes the very means of recovery.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps ransomware recovery to isolation + clean offline backups.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware

questions.question: Which TWO are recognized anti-malware scanning modes? (Select TWO.)

explanation.why_correct: On-access (real-time) and on-demand (scheduled/manual) are the two anti-malware scanning modes.

why_others_are_wrong.A: "On-vacation scanning" is not a real mode.
why_others_are_wrong.D: "On-paper scanning" is not an anti-malware mode.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies anti-malware scanning modes.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Types of Malware Scanning

questions.question: Which TWO elements are essential components of a useful log entry for investigations? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: An accurate timestamp of when the event occurred

options.label: B
options.text: The marketing slogan of the company

options.label: C
options.text: The color of the server chassis

options.label: D
options.text: The source/identity associated with the event

explanation.why_correct: Accurate timestamps (synchronized time) and the source/identity tied to the event are essential so activity can be correlated and attributed during investigations.

why_others_are_wrong.B: A slogan is irrelevant to log analysis.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Chassis color is irrelevant.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies essential log-entry components.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Essential Components of Log Entries

questions.question: Running software that has reached End of Life (EOL)/End of Support (EOS) is a security risk because:

options.label: A
options.text: It automatically gains new security features

options.label: C
options.text: The vendor no longer issues security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities unfixed

options.label: D
options.text: It cannot run on any hardware

explanation.why_correct: EOL/EOS software stops receiving vendor security updates, so newly discovered vulnerabilities remain unpatched—such systems should be replaced or isolated.

why_others_are_wrong.A: EOL/EOS removes support; it does not add features.
why_others_are_wrong.D: EOL software may still run; the risk is lack of patches.
why_others_are_wrong.B: EOL software does not self-encrypt for protection.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the unpatched-vulnerability risk of EOL/EOS software.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > End of Life (EOL) and End of Support (EOS)

questions.question: The defensive value of the Cyber Kill Chain model is that:

options.label: A
options.text: It guarantees attacks can never succeed

options.label: B
options.text: It is a wireless encryption protocol

options.label: C
options.text: It only applies to physical security

options.label: D
options.text: Disrupting any single stage can break the attack before the adversary achieves their objective

explanation.why_correct: Because an intrusion must progress through ordered stages, defenders who detect and disrupt any stage can stop the attack before its final objective.

why_others_are_wrong.A: No model guarantees prevention of all attacks.
why_others_are_wrong.B: It is an intrusion model, not wireless encryption.
why_others_are_wrong.C: It applies to cyber intrusions broadly, not only physical security.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the disrupt-any-stage defensive concept of the kill chain.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Cyber Kill Chain

questions.question: Spyware is distinguished from adware in that spyware primarily:

options.label: A
options.text: Displays unwanted advertisements to generate revenue

options.label: D
options.text: Covertly gathers information about a user without consent

explanation.why_correct: Spyware covertly collects user information/activity; adware focuses on displaying unwanted advertisements.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Displaying ads describes adware.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Encrypting for ransom describes ransomware.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Backup power is unrelated.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes spyware (surveillance) from adware (ads).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Detective and Preventative Measures > Additional Malware Types

questions.question: Using automation to create, manage, or destroy configuration items consistently helps security by:

options.label: A
options.text: Removing the need for any baseline

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing manual errors and enforcing consistent, repeatable secure configurations

explanation.why_correct: Automated provisioning enforces consistent, repeatable configurations (from baselines), reducing manual error and configuration drift.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Automation relies on baselines as references.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Untracked ad-hoc changes undermine configuration management.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Automation should operate within change control, not replace it.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the consistency benefit of provisioning automation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Configuration Management > Provisioning and Automation

questions.question: Order the incident management steps as listed in the (ISC)² CBK. (Provide the option labels in order.)

explanation.why_correct: The CBK incident management steps are: Detection, Response, Mitigation, Reporting, Recovery, Remediation, and Lessons Learned.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the ordered CBK incident management steps.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Incident Management Steps (CBK)

questions.question: In the NIST incident response model, the Preparation phase includes:

options.label: A
options.text: Establishing the IR policy, forming the incident response team, and deploying tools (IDS, DLP, etc.)

explanation.why_correct: Preparation establishes the incident response policy, defines incidents/priorities, forms the IR team with roles/contacts, and deploys necessary tools before incidents occur.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Eradication occurs during containment/eradication/recovery, not preparation.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The lessons-learned report is post-incident activity.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Restoring from backup is part of recovery.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the contents of the NIST Preparation phase.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Incident Management Steps (NIST Mapping)

questions.question: A SOC analyst receives many alerts and must determine which represent genuine incidents requiring response. This analysis/prioritization activity is called:

explanation.why_correct: Triage analyzes and prioritizes events to confirm genuine incidents and determine response urgency during the detection/analysis phase.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Remediation addresses root causes after response.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Lessons learned is the post-incident review.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Provisioning is an identity/configuration activity.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps event analysis/prioritization to triage.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Detection and Analysis

questions.question: The PRIMARY purpose of the lessons-learned (post-incident) phase is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Assign blame to a single employee

options.label: C
options.text: Analyze how the incident was handled and improve future response plans/controls

explanation.why_correct: Lessons learned reviews incident handling, identifies gaps and root causes, and drives improvements to plans, controls, and processes.

why_others_are_wrong.A: The goal is improvement, not blame assignment.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Logs should be retained, not deleted, for analysis and evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Paying ransom is not the purpose of lessons learned.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the improvement focus of lessons learned.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Lessons Learned

questions.question: Active malware is spreading laterally across the network during an incident. After detection/analysis, what is the MOST immediate priority?

options.label: A
options.text: Contain/mitigate the spread (e.g., isolate affected systems) to limit damage

options.label: B
options.text: Conduct the annual security awareness training

explanation.why_correct: Once an incident is confirmed and spreading, containment/mitigation (isolating affected systems) is the immediate priority to limit damage before eradication and recovery.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Reporting/executive summaries come after stabilizing the situation.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Awareness training is not an immediate incident-response action.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Scheduling future tests does not address the active incident.

questions.exam_reasoning: Prioritizes containment/mitigation during active spread.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Detection and Analysis

questions.question: An inquiry into whether an organization complied with a specific industry regulator's rules is which type of investigation?

explanation.why_correct: A regulatory investigation examines compliance with a regulator's rules/standards for an industry.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Administrative investigations address internal policy matters.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Criminal investigations pursue violations of criminal law.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Civil investigations concern disputes between private parties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes regulatory from other investigation types.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Investigations

questions.question: A cyber case may be pursued criminally (risking imprisonment) or civilly (seeking damages). Which correctly pairs each with its standard of proof?

options.label: A
options.text: Both use preponderance of the evidence

options.label: B
options.text: Both use beyond a reasonable doubt

options.label: C
options.text: Criminal = beyond a reasonable doubt; Civil = preponderance of the evidence

options.label: D
options.text: Criminal = preponderance of the evidence; Civil = beyond a reasonable doubt

explanation.why_correct: Criminal cases require the higher "beyond a reasonable doubt" standard; civil cases use the lower "preponderance of the evidence" standard.

why_others_are_wrong.D: This reverses the two standards.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Civil cases use the lower preponderance standard, not beyond a reasonable doubt.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Criminal cases use the higher beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests criminal vs civil standards of proof.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Burden of Proof Standards

questions.question: An internal investigation into a suspected violation of company policy, used to support an HR decision, is a(n):

explanation.why_correct: Administrative investigations address internal policy violations and inform organizational/HR decisions.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Criminal investigations involve law enforcement and criminal law.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Regulatory investigations concern compliance with a regulator.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Civil investigations involve disputes between parties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps an internal policy inquiry to an administrative investigation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Investigations

questions.question: Modus Operandi (MO) analysis in an investigation focuses on:

options.label: A
options.text: The brand of the victim's laptop

options.label: C
options.text: The attacker's characteristic methods/patterns of operation

explanation.why_correct: MO analysis studies the attacker's characteristic methods and patterns, which can help attribute or anticipate behavior.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Laptop brand is not the focus of MO analysis.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Floor plans are unrelated to MO.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Marketing budgets are irrelevant.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the meaning of MO analysis.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Investigations

questions.question: The "best evidence rule" generally requires that:

options.label: C
options.text: Evidence be destroyed after the case

options.label: D
options.text: Original documents/evidence be used whenever possible (copies are secondary and may be inadmissible)

explanation.why_correct: The best evidence rule favors original documents/evidence; copies are secondary and can be challenged for authenticity.

why_others_are_wrong.A: The rule prefers originals over copies, not the reverse.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The rule is about document originals, not testimony precedence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Evidence must be preserved, not destroyed.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the best evidence rule (prefer originals).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Key Evidence Rules

questions.question: Hearsay evidence is:

options.label: A
options.text: Information relayed from someone who did not directly witness the event

options.label: C
options.text: A witness's account of something they personally observed

options.label: D
options.text: Physical evidence collected at the scene

explanation.why_correct: Hearsay is secondhand information from someone who did not directly witness the event, and is often subject to admissibility limits.

why_others_are_wrong.C: A firsthand account is direct evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.B: An expert opinion is opinion evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Physical scene evidence is not testimonial hearsay.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the definition of hearsay evidence.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Testimonial Evidence

questions.question: Video footage that supports and verifies the access logs already collected is an example of which evidence type?

explanation.why_correct: Corroborative evidence supports or verifies other evidence (e.g., video footage alongside access logs), strengthening a case.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Circumstantial evidence implies a fact indirectly rather than verifying existing evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Hearsay is secondhand information.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Opinion evidence is an expert's professional judgment.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps supporting/verifying evidence to corroborative evidence.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Additional Evidence Types

questions.question: Direct evidence is BEST described as:

options.label: C
options.text: Facts that only imply an event occurred

options.label: D
options.text: Witness testimony based on firsthand observation

explanation.why_correct: Direct evidence is testimony from a witness who personally observed the event.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Secondhand non-witness information is hearsay.
why_others_are_wrong.B: An expert opinion is opinion evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Indirectly implied facts are circumstantial evidence.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of direct evidence.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Testimonial Evidence

questions.question: A laptop seized as evidence is later challenged in court because no one can prove who handled it between seizure and analysis. Which control was inadequately maintained?

explanation.why_correct: Chain of custody documents who handled evidence, when, and how—an unbroken, documented chain is required to preserve evidentiary integrity and admissibility.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Load balancing distributes traffic; it is unrelated to evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Whitelisting is a preventative software control.
why_others_are_wrong.D: QoS prioritizes network traffic, unrelated to evidence handling.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps unprovable evidence handling to a broken chain of custody.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Chain of Custody

questions.question: Which TWO are recognized types of testimonial evidence? (Select TWO.)

explanation.why_correct: Direct evidence (firsthand observation) and opinion evidence (expert judgment) are testimonial evidence types, along with hearsay.

why_others_are_wrong.B: "Failover evidence" is not an evidence type (failover is a recovery technique).
why_others_are_wrong.A: "Whitelisted evidence" is not an evidence type.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies testimonial evidence types.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Types of Testimonial Evidence

questions.question: Order the core digital forensic process stages within incident response. (Provide the option labels in order.)

explanation.why_correct: The forensic process proceeds: Collection (acquire evidence), Examination (extract relevant data), Analysis (interpret findings), and Reporting (document conclusions).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the ordered forensic process stages.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Forensic Process in Incident Response

questions.question: During live evidence collection on a running system, which data should generally be captured FIRST to avoid losing it?

options.label: A
options.text: Archived backup tapes in off-site storage

options.label: B
options.text: Printed documents in a filing cabinet

options.label: C
options.text: Volatile data such as RAM contents and active network connections

explanation.why_correct: The order of volatility dictates collecting the most volatile data first (e.g., RAM, running processes, network connections) before it is lost, then less-volatile media.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Off-site backup tapes are non-volatile and can be collected later.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Printed documents are static and not volatile.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Powered-off drives retain data and are less volatile than RAM.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the order-of-volatility principle in forensics.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Forensic Process in Incident Response

questions.question: Digital forensics, when applied to identifying electronic evidence for legal proceedings, is also referred to as:

explanation.why_correct: Digital forensics for legal evidence is also called eDiscovery/electronic data discovery, following a structured reference model (EDRM).

why_others_are_wrong.B: Load balancing distributes traffic.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Whitelisting is a preventative control.
why_others_are_wrong.D: QoS prioritizes network traffic.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps electronic legal-evidence discovery to eDiscovery.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Digital Forensics

questions.question: To analyze a compromised hard drive forensically while keeping the evidence admissible, an investigator should:

options.label: A
options.text: Boot and use the original drive directly to save time

options.label: C
options.text: Share the drive freely without documentation

options.label: D
options.text: Work from a forensic image/copy and protect the original, maintaining chain of custody

explanation.why_correct: Forensic best practice analyzes a verified bit-for-bit image (often with write-blocking), preserving the original and documenting chain of custody to maintain integrity/admissibility.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Using the original directly risks altering evidence and breaking admissibility.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Reformatting destroys the evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Undocumented sharing breaks chain of custody.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests image-and-preserve forensic practice.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Purpose of Digital Forensics

questions.question: The reporting stage of a digital forensic investigation emphasizes:

options.label: A
options.text: Accuracy and authenticity, presenting admissible evidence with clear explanations

explanation.why_correct: Forensic reporting focuses on accuracy/authenticity, documenting how conclusions were reached and presenting admissible evidence clearly (e.g., for court).

why_others_are_wrong.B: Sacrificing correctness undermines admissibility.
why_others_are_wrong.D: The methodology must be documented, not omitted.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Evidence must be preserved, not deleted.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests forensic reporting emphasis on accuracy/admissibility.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Digital Forensic Incident Response

questions.question: Forming an Incident Response Team (IRT) with defined roles and contacts BEFORE an incident occurs is part of which phase?

explanation.why_correct: Establishing the IR team, roles, responsibilities, and contacts is a Preparation activity, done before incidents occur.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Recovery restores normal operations after an incident.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Lessons learned is a post-incident review.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Remediation fixes root causes after response.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps IR team formation to the Preparation phase.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Incident Management Steps (NIST Mapping)

questions.question: Which TWO are recognized evidence collection techniques in investigations? (Select TWO.)

explanation.why_correct: Interviewing and surveillance (along with interrogation and digital forensics) are recognized evidence collection techniques.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Disabling logging destroys potential evidence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Deleting suspect files destroys evidence.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies valid evidence-collection techniques.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Evidence Collection Techniques

questions.question: A key consideration for forensic investigations is that investigators should:

options.label: A
options.text: Be competent, follow consistent policy/process, and maintain chain of custody

options.label: C
options.text: Avoid documenting any of their steps

explanation.why_correct: Forensic investigators should be competent, aware of data sources, and follow consistent policies/processes while maintaining chain of custody for admissibility.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Improvising without procedures undermines repeatability and admissibility.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Steps must be documented for the evidence to hold up.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Accountability and documented handling are essential.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests forensic investigator best practices.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Considerations for Forensic Investigations

questions.question: In the guide's model, a security investigation is typically INITIATED by:

options.label: C
options.text: The incident response process identifying an event that warrants investigation

explanation.why_correct: Incident response initiates the investigation when an event is detected/confirmed that requires deeper inquiry (administrative, civil, criminal, or regulatory).

why_others_are_wrong.D: Marketing campaigns do not trigger security investigations.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Budget approval is unrelated.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Office cleaning is unrelated.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects investigation initiation to incident response.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Incident Management > Investigation Process

questions.question: Opinion evidence is provided by:

options.label: A
options.text: A witness who saw the event firsthand

options.label: C

questions.question: A small nonprofit with a tight budget can tolerate several days of downtime for its non-critical systems. Which recovery site is the MOST cost-appropriate?

options.label: B
options.text: Two hot sites in different regions

explanation.why_correct: When days of downtime are acceptable and budget is tight, a cold site (cheapest, slowest) is the cost-appropriate choice.

why_others_are_wrong.D: A hot site is the most expensive—overkill for non-critical, downtime-tolerant systems.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Active-active data centers are very costly and unnecessary here.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Two hot sites is the most expensive option, far exceeding the need.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps budget-constrained, downtime-tolerant needs to a cold site.

questions.question: Which is broader in scope?

options.label: C
options.text: Disaster Recovery (DR), which is broader than BC

options.label: D
options.text: Business Continuity (BC), which encompasses keeping the whole business running

explanation.why_correct: BC is the broader discipline (people, processes, facilities, and IT) of keeping the business running; DR is the narrower IT-restoration component.

why_others_are_wrong.C: DR is a subset of BC, not broader.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Their scopes differ.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Both address business operations/continuity in different scopes.

questions.question: The risk assessment within a BIA evaluates:

options.label: B
options.text: The probability and impact of threat events affecting critical assets

explanation.why_correct: A BIA's risk assessment evaluates the probability and impact of threat events on critical assets/processes (qualitatively and/or quantitatively).

why_others_are_wrong.A: Coffee consumption is irrelevant.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Marketing metrics are unrelated to BIA risk.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Dashboard colors are irrelevant.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the probability/impact focus of BIA risk assessment.

questions.question: Conceptually, disaster recovery activities tend to focus on the ____, while business continuity focuses on the ____.

options.label: C
options.text: Restoration of IT after the event; keeping critical functions running throughout

explanation.why_correct: DR concentrates on restoring IT systems/infrastructure after a disaster; BC focuses on sustaining critical business functions throughout the disruption.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Marketing/hiring plans are not the BC/DR distinction.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Coffee/parking are irrelevant.
why_others_are_wrong.D: SSIDs/firewall rules are network specifics, not the BC/DR distinction.

questions.exam_reasoning: Reinforces the DR (restore IT) vs BC (sustain functions) distinction.

questions.question: Building redundancy into critical systems primarily protects which security property?

explanation.why_correct: Redundancy (clusters, redundant power, multiple sites) primarily supports availability by removing single points of failure.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Confidentiality concerns disclosure, not redundancy.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Non-repudiation concerns proof of origin.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Anonymity is unrelated to redundancy.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps redundancy to availability.

questions.question: An organization maintains a warm site but has never tested restoring its backups there. What is the MOST significant risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Backups may fail to restore at the site when a real disaster strikes

options.label: B
options.text: The MTD will no longer matter

options.label: C
options.text: The warm site will become a hot site automatically

options.label: D
options.text: The RPO will drop to zero on its own

explanation.why_correct: Untested backups/recovery procedures may not actually restore at the warm site during a real disaster—testing is essential to validate recoverability.

why_others_are_wrong.C: A warm site does not automatically upgrade to a hot site.
why_others_are_wrong.D: RPO does not improve to zero without changes to backup strategy.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The MTD remains the business constraint regardless.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the risk of untested backups/recovery at a site.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery > Data Backup Strategies

questions.question: Training, education, and regular exercises in a continuity program help ensure that:

why_others_are_wrong.A: Plans must be updated as the environment changes.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Backups remain essential.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Marketing quotas are unrelated.

questions.question: A BIA risk assessment that ranks impacts using categories like high/medium/low (rather than dollar figures) is:

explanation.why_correct: A qualitative assessment ranks risk using subjective categories (high/medium/low); a quantitative assessment uses numeric/monetary values.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Quantitative assessment uses numeric/monetary values.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A penetration test is an offensive security assessment.

questions.question: An audit finds the entire e-commerce platform depends on one database server with no redundancy. This is BEST described as:

options.label: A
options.text: An acceptable design requiring no change

options.label: B
options.text: A single point of failure that should be mitigated with redundancy/clustering

options.label: C
options.text: A form of separation of duties

explanation.why_correct: A lone, non-redundant critical component is a single point of failure; redundancy (clustering, replication, failover) mitigates the availability risk.

why_others_are_wrong.A: A critical SPOF is a risk that should be addressed, not accepted as-is.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Redundancy concerns availability, not confidentiality.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Separation of duties is an access/authorization control, unrelated here.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps a lone critical component to a single point of failure.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 7 > Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery > Server Protection

questions.question: Disaster recovery strategies include both short-term and long-term techniques because:

options.label: A
options.text: Recovery should never be planned in advance

options.label: B
options.text: Short-term and long-term mean exactly the same thing

options.label: D
options.text: Immediate measures stabilize operations while longer-term efforts fully restore normal capability

explanation.why_correct: DR uses short-term measures to stabilize/resume critical functions quickly and longer-term efforts to fully restore normal operations.

why_others_are_wrong.B: They address different time horizons of recovery.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Both short- and long-term recovery are important.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Recovery must be planned in advance to be effective.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the short-term/long-term recovery distinction.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Certificate issuance is a PKI function.
